newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX ACCESS gasoline prices sink with API build.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX ACCESS gasoline prices sink with API build.

text.p: U.S. gasoline futures sank after a bearish floor session Tuesday, hit late by news of big inventories builds at U.S. refineries last week, traders said.
Trade group American Petroleum Institute (API) released its weekly crude and refined product inventory report showing increases in crude oil, gasoline, and distillates for the week ended December 6.
Gasoline rose a huge 5.9 million barrels last week to 19.4 million, according to API
After-hours, January gasoline lopped off 1.01 cents from its settlement to trade 65.85 cents a gallon. About 129 lots traded in the front-month and 229 overall.
"What it's really keying off of its distillates," a California-based trader said.
Late Tuesday, API reported stocks of heating oil rose 2.1 million barrels last week, pressuring the January futures contract down 0.92 cents a gallon to 68.70 cents on ACCESS.
Pressure also came from forecasts of milder temperatures for the high-consumption U.S. Northeast market.
"We're not being hit with an exceptionally cold winter and refiners are able to play catch-up," one California-based trader said.
About 321 lots of January heating oil traded, with 418 exchanged in all months.
January crude, which saw a slight build of 324,000 barrels, fell 18 cents a barrel to $24.24 as 833 lots traded.
